newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on Lujiazui fall.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on Lujiazui fall.

text.p: Shanghai B shares dipped on Wednesday on falls of Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development but selling of most stocks was impossible with few buyers, brokers said.
The index slipped 0.351 points or 0.74 percent to 47.303 points, on volume of 3.6 million shares worth $1.5 million. Of 41 B shares, 29 traded, with 10 down, 11 flat and eight up.

Brokers said the market fell with heavy liquidation of Shanghai Lujiazui who will offer a three-for-10 rights issue early next month, but trading of most stocks was slow because few investors were interested in the market.
Shanghai Lujaizui traded the second most, dropping $0.016 or 1.81 percent to $0.864, on volume of 704,700 shares.
"Selling of market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui pushed the index down, but trading was slow because liquidation of other stocks was impossible due to few buying orders," one broker said.
"Given the current poor market sentiment, the index is likely to test a historic low of 46.857 points soon if there is no big positive news," another broker said.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on liquidation, falling $0.008 or 7.27 percent to $0.102, on volume of 70,000 shares.
Speculative stock Shanghai New Asia Group traded the most on intra-institutional trading, ending unchanged at $0.480 on volume of 782,000 shares.

Shanghai A shares plunged on rumours that the securities authorities would shortly announce new measures to crack down on trading on credit and a new quota for share issues which would quicken the pace of market expansion, brokers said.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.

The A index closed down 62.766 points or 5.85 percent to 1009.351 points, on volume of 795.0 million shares worth 7.2 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index dipped 130.055 points or 4.88 percent to 2535.017 points.
Shanghai Shenhua Electronics was the biggest loser on heavy profit-taking after jumping 8.00 yuan in the past weeks, brokers said.
It tumbled 3.52 yuan or 13.53 percent to 22.48 yuan, on volume of 12.4 million shares.
